transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what brings me in is I feel like I’m constantly running on a motor lately. Like at school, I’ll finish one thing and before I’ve even really stopped, I’m already jumping into the next thing, and then the same thing happens at home.

I’m a special education teacher, so there’s always something going on anyway — paperwork, students needing support, little fires to put out — and I’ve always been busy, but this feels different. It’s like I can’t shut myself off. I’ll get home and instead of sitting down, I’m immediately doing something else, and then something after that. It’s exhausting, but I still keep going.
Have you noticed any time recently where your mood was unusually high, overly irritable, or you felt extremely confident or energetic, even to the point where others might have commented on it?

I don’t know… I don’t think so? I mean, I get wound up, sure, but “unusually high” or like overly confident—no, I wouldn’t say that. Irritable maybe just in the normal sense, like when the copier breaks at school or someone schedules another meeting during planning time, which happens all the time, and then you’re trying to track down a paraeducator and—

Sorry, I’m getting off track. I don’t think people have said I seemed unusually high or anything like that. More like I’m just… always going.
Have you noticed that you need less sleep lately, like you feel rested even if you haven’t slept much?

I’m not sure I’d say I need less sleep, exactly. I mean, my sleep hasn’t been great forever, but feeling rested on just a few hours? No, I don’t think so.

If anything, when I don’t sleep much, I feel it the next day. Though at school you kind of have to keep moving anyway because there’s always a student needing something or a meeting starting and—sorry. But no, I haven’t noticed that I’m suddenly fine with less sleep.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or unable to sit still, maybe moving around more than usual without realizing it, like fidgeting, pacing, or feeling like you're always on edge?

Yeah, definitely. I don’t even always notice I’m doing it until someone kind of looks over.

Like in IEP meetings, or even in my admin classes, my leg will be bouncing under the table the whole time, or I’m clicking a pen, or shifting around in the chair. And those meetings can already be long, you know, with the paperwork and everyone trying to get on the same page, and then I’ll realize I’ve been moving nonstop because someone glances at me.

So yes, sitting still is hard. It’s like my body is doing something before I’ve caught up to it.
Have you noticed your thoughts feeling especially fast or racing lately, like one idea quickly leads to another and it’s hard to keep up?

I don’t know if I’d call it racing, exactly. My mind does jump around, like I’ll be thinking about one thing and then remember three other things I’m supposed to do, and then suddenly I’m thinking about a student’s schedule or whether I replied to an email, and then—well, that happens a lot at work.

But “especially fast lately,” I’m not sure. It’s hard to tell because my brain kind of always feels busy. I haven’t noticed some big new thing where my thoughts are going so fast I can’t keep up, if that’s what you mean.
Have you been taking on more projects or responsibilities lately, like starting new tasks or making big plans, more than you typically would?

Yeah, I mean… I don’t know if I’d say “big plans” exactly, but I am constantly taking on the next thing. That’s actually a lot of why I came in.

It feels like I’m running on a motor lately. I finish something at school, and before I’ve even really finished-finished it, I’m already starting the next thing. Same at home. I’ll get one thing done and immediately jump to another, and then another, and I can’t seem to shut myself off.

And in special ed there’s always something, you know—forms, meetings, a student needing help, someone stopping by the room—and I just keep moving from one thing to the next. So yes, more in the sense that I can’t stop picking things up or moving on to the next responsibility, even when I probably should pause.
Have you had any days where you felt down, depressed, or hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even for a little while?

I’m not sure… I don’t think so, not in the way you mean. I get worn out, sure, especially after school days when it’s one meeting after another and you’re trying to track paperwork and parents and schedules—like yesterday I was looking for one form and ended up reorganizing a whole folder because it was bothering me—

But depressed or hopeless? I don’t know. I wouldn’t say that’s really been the thing. And I still like the things I like, when I actually stop long enough to do them. So… no, I haven’t really noticed days like that.
Have you noticed that you can stay up late and still feel completely alert and energized the next day, even without much sleep?

I don’t think so. I mean, I do stay up later than I should sometimes, but the next day I’m usually aware of it. Like, I’ll get to school and I’m moving around because that’s just the job—there’s always someone needing something—and then I’ll realize I forgot to print something or I’m standing in the copy room thinking, “What did I come in here for?”

But completely alert and energized without sleep? No, I wouldn’t say that. I might push through because I have to, but I don’t feel magically fine or anything.
Have you had a period lasting several days where your mood was clearly different from usual, like feeling unusually excited, wired, or irritable in a way that stood out to you or others?

I don’t think I’ve had a several-days thing like that, no. I mean, I get wound up during the day sometimes—especially at school, because one kid needs something, then there’s a meeting, then somebody asks about paperwork, and suddenly I’m halfway through three things at once.

But as far as my mood being clearly different for days, like unusually excited or irritable where people would say, “What’s going on with you?”… I haven’t really noticed that. Or nobody’s told me that, anyway. I’m just kind of… busy and hard to slow down, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing you mean.
Can you think of a time when you felt so full of energy or so unusually upbeat or irritable that it was noticeably different from your usual self, even for a few days in a row?

Not really, no. I mean, I can get keyed up, especially if the day is packed and people keep coming at me with questions—like at school, it’s never just one thing, it’s “Can you look at this IEP?” and “Did you call that parent?” and then someone stops me in the hallway and I’m already thinking about three other things.

But a few days in a row where I’m unusually upbeat or irritable, like different from myself? I don’t think so. I’d probably notice if people were reacting to me like that, or my wife would say something. I haven’t really had that kind of stretch that I can think of.
Can you think of a time when your mood was so noticeably different—like unusually upbeat, elevated, or irritable—that it affected how you functioned, even for just a few days?

I’m trying to think of one, but no, not really. I mean, I’ve had days where I’m more wound up or snappy than I want to be, but it’s usually because the day is chaotic—like at school, if the schedule changes three times and people are asking me things in the hallway, I can get kind of… short, I guess.

But a few days where my mood was noticeably different, like upbeat or elevated or irritable enough that it changed how I functioned? I don’t think so. My functioning gets messy sometimes, but I don’t think it’s because my mood suddenly shifted like that. It’s more like I’m juggling too much and then I lose track of what I was doing.
Can you think of a time when your mood was so noticeably different—like unusually upbeat, elevated, or irritable—that it affected how you functioned, even for just a few days?

I’m not coming up with one, honestly. I know I can have bad days where I’m kind of revved up or irritated, but it doesn’t feel like a whole “mood shift” thing for a few days.

Like, if I’m at school and I’m trying to get through paperwork and someone interrupts me—well, that happens constantly, and then I’ll lose my place, and then I’m annoyed because I had it in my head and it’s gone. And then I’ll go to the copy room and forget why I went there, which is ridiculous, but also kind of normal for my day.

But as far as being unusually upbeat or elevated, or so irritable that it was clearly different from me and affected everything for a few days… no, I don’t think so. I think it’s more just day-to-day getting pulled in too many directions.

Can you think of a time when your mood was clearly different from your usual self, even for just a day or two—like feeling unusually upbeat, irritable, or energized in a way that stood out to you or others?

I’m still not really thinking of anything like that. I mean, I can be energetic in the normal sense—well, “normal” for me, I guess—but not like a clear day or two where everyone would say, “What’s going on with him?”

Sometimes people at school say, “You’re all over the place today,” but that’s usually because I’m bouncing between things, or someone catches me between classes and then I start answering before I’ve even finished the last thing I was doing. Like yesterday I went to grab something from the office and ended up talking to three different people and forgot the thing I went for—so I might look revved up, I suppose.

But mood-wise, like unusually upbeat or irritable in a way that stood out? I don’t think so. Not that I can point to.

Can you think of a time when you had a stretch of at least several days—like four or more days in a row—where your mood was clearly different from usual, such as feeling unusually upbeat, high, or irritable in a way that others might have noticed?

Four days in a row… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I’d probably remember if people were noticing I was really different for that long.

I do have days where I’m kind of keyed up, but then again, school can do that to anybody. Like when we have an assembly schedule and then half the kids come in late and I’ve got three emails I forgot to answer—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

But no, I can’t think of a stretch of several days where my mood was unusually high or irritable in a way that stood out. Nothing like that comes to mind.

But no, I can’t think of a stretch of several days where my mood was unusually high or irritable in a way that stood out. Nothing like that comes to mind.

inference.note: The patient has consistently denied experiencing episodes of elevated mood, increased energy with reduced need for sleep, or a persistently irritable mood lasting several days, which makes F43.22 (Adjustment Disorder with Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood) less likely. The clinical picture remains consistent with F90.0 (Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Type). No further differentials remain under consideration.
